debate.text: Thornley Reach lost £43m on its own housing company, and I signed nothing. A sells tenants' homes, B cuts adult social care and makes tenants pay too, C leaves the books open until a grant turns up. Twelve citizens said keep every red line, 6 to 4. I agree. Nobody loses their keys for a company they never voted on.

Bea, the citizens asked who signed the loan, and that is the right question. A £74m lend with no name on it is not a mistake, it is a decision nobody has to answer for. Publish the name before Wednesday's vote. People feel safer when somebody is answerable.

Answer B names adult social care for cuts, three years running. I have watched what a lost care visit does: a fall, then a bed on my ward. It costs more in the end. I back the red line. Nobody should pay for a building scheme with an old person's care.

Hang on. Rejecting all three leaves a council that has to balance its books by law by Wednesday. 'Keep looking' is not a plan, Bea. Finishing 410 half-built homes means paid work for builders, so someone must name a buyer and a date. Bring me a route that breaks none.

Fair, Callum. That is why it goes back, not into the bin. The test is plain: balance the books, keep tenants in their homes, leave care alone, and name who signed. Find one answer that does all four and I will sign it.
